elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section (b) applies the cap to “EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY.”

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap includes fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Section (b) includes only fees actually “PAID” in the preceding 12 months and omits fees payable.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the fee-based limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The redline contains no USD 1,000,000 floor and no greater-of formulation.

elements.element: Special, indirect, incidental, or consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Section (a) excludes these damages only for Licensor; it does not protect Licensee on a mutual basis.

elements.element: Each party's liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly makes each party's liability uncapped for breach of its confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Each party's liability for breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No carve-out addresses data protection obligations.

elements.element: Each party's liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped.
Each party's liability for indemnification obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly makes each party's liability uncapped for its indemnification obligations.

elements.element: Each party's liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly makes each party's liability uncapped for gross negligence.

elements.element: Each party's liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly makes each party's liability uncapped for “WILLFUL MISCONDUCT,” which is substantively equivalent to wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Each party's liability for fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Fraud is not included in the carve-outs.

elements.element: Each party's liability for infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No such carve-out is included. Section (a) instead broadly disclaims Licensor liability for claims that use of the technology infringes any person's rights.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are expressly excluded from damages subject to the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause does not state that Licensee's payment obligations are not damages or otherwise exclude them from the cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section (b) caps “EITHER PARTY'S” aggregate cumulative total liability.

elements.element: The mutual cap is measured by 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section (b) sets the cap at fees paid by Licensee in the 12 months preceding the claim.

elements.element: Each party's indemnification obligations are carved out of the cap.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly states that the cap does not apply to each party's indemnification obligations.

elements.element: Each party's liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out of the cap.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly states that the cap does not apply to each party's breach of its confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Each party's liability for gross negligence is carved out of the cap.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly states that the cap does not apply to each party's gross negligence.

elements.element: Each party's liability for wilful misconduct is carved out of the cap.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly states that the cap does not apply to each party's “WILLFUL MISCONDUCT.”

result.reason: The operative redline reaches the fallback by making the 12-month-fee cap mutual and adding all four required mutual carve-outs. It does not reach the preferred position because it lacks the USD 1,000,000 floor, payable-fee language, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, several required carve-outs, and the payment-obligations clarification. The changes are limited to the fallback requirements, but drafting quality remains mediocre due to the inherited run-on language, inconsistent capitalization, placement of the carve-out after subsection (c), and the continuing one-sided and unusually broad Licensor exclusions.
